clue.text: He-cat, eh? Possibly

indicators.note: 'possibly' suggests the letters before it are only one of several possible arrangements

blocks.note: the seven letters of these words, used as fodder

explanation.surface: Someone peers at a big spotted animal and wonders whether it is a male cat.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is both the wordplay and the definition: a cheetah may indeed be a he-cat.
explanation.definitionFit: A cheetah is a big cat, and a male one is literally a he-cat, so the clue describes it in full.

clue.text: Unwell after cold hotel — could be this

definitions.text: Unwell after cold hotel — could be this

indicators.note: 'after' places the word for unwell behind the pieces that come before it

blocks.note: C is the abbreviation for cold, as on a tap
H is hotel in the NATO phonetic alphabet
a plain synonym

explanation.surface: A guest feels ill after staying in a cold hotel and wonders what caught them.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue doubles as the definition: being unwell after a cold hotel could well be this mild illness.
explanation.definitionFit: A chill is a mild feverish illness caused by exposure to cold, just what a freezing hotel might give you.

clue.text: Book making new use of cyclopean idea?

indicators.note: putting letters to a new use means rearranging them into something different

blocks.note: the thirteen letters of these two words

explanation.surface: A writer wonders whether their book takes a giant, one-eyed idea in a fresh direction.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cyclopean' means gigantic or one-eyed, after the Cyclops; here it is only a bag of letters.
explanation.definitionFit: An encyclopaedia is a reference book of articles covering many subjects.

clue.text: Dance from part of east Angola

indicators.note: the answer is only a part of the words that follow, sitting inside them

blocks.note: found running across the two words

explanation.surface: A dance traditional to the eastern region of Angola.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer is the last letter of east and the first four of Angola.
explanation.definitionFit: The tango is a ballroom dance that originated in Argentina.

clue.text: Queen perhaps ordered throne

indicators.note: 'ordered' says the letters are put into a fresh order

blocks.note: the six letters of this word

explanation.surface: A queen, perhaps, gave orders concerning her throne.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Queen' and 'throne' paint royalty; the queen is the egg-laying female of an insect colony.
explanation.definitionFit: A hornet colony is founded by a queen, so a queen is an example of this stinging wasp.

clue.text: Type of book work embraced by young boxer?

indicators.note: something embraced is held in the arms, so one piece sits inside the other

blocks.note: a boxer is a breed of dog, and a young dog is a pup
OP is short for opus, a work

explanation.surface: A book about a young boxer's training, with his work hugged by the coach.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Boxer' suggests a fighter, but it is the dog breed.
explanation.definitionFit: A pop-up book has pictures that rise from the page when it is opened, so it is a type of book.

clue.text: Blasphemous university academic article on ecstasy

indicators.note: in a down clue 'on' places the later piece beneath the one before it

blocks.note: short for professor
the indefinite article
E is slang for the drug ecstasy

explanation.surface: A university lecturer is accused of blasphemy over an article about ecstasy.
explanation.definitionFit: Profane means showing disrespect for sacred things, which is what blasphemous means.

clue.text: After classical show musical mostly returns, just having left theatre

indicators.note: 'mostly' means nearly all, so the final letter of the musical's name is dropped
something that returns goes back the way it came, so it is read backwards

blocks.note: the Latin prefix meaning after
an opera is a classical stage show
the Lloyd Webber and Rice musical about Eva Perón

explanation.surface: After the opera a musical comes back to the stage, just after the audience has left the theatre.
explanation.walkthrough: The theatre is the operating theatre, not a playhouse; 'classical show' and 'musical' push the stage reading.
explanation.definitionFit: Post-operative describes the period immediately after surgery, when a patient has just been taken out of the operating theatre.

clue.text: Reward any temp might work for?

indicators.note: letters that work are worked over, kneaded into a different arrangement

blocks.note: the seven letters of these two words

explanation.surface: What a temporary worker hopes to earn for their labour.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface also defines it: a temp works for wages.
explanation.definitionFit: Payment is money given in return for work, a reward for services.

clue.text: Home game in Congo university takes cunning so as to stand out?

indicators.note: 'in' places the game inside the country's name

blocks.note: at home means in
taken as written
RU is rugby union
U is the abbreviation for university
a plain synonym

explanation.surface: A home match in the Congo where the university side wins by sheer cunning.
explanation.walkthrough: The game sits between the fourth and fifth letters of Congo. The question mark flags a loose definition: doing something out of place makes it stand out.
explanation.definitionFit: Something done incongruously is out of keeping with its surroundings, so it sticks out.

clue.text: Type of sugar in cola set to change

indicators.note: letters set to change are about to be altered into a new order

blocks.note: the seven letters of these two words

explanation.surface: The kind of sugar in a fizzy cola is about to be reformulated.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests cola's sweetener, but that sugar is found in milk.
explanation.definitionFit: Lactose is the sugar naturally present in milk.

clue.text: Brick for building half done in Lincoln?

indicators.note: only half of the following word is kept, the back two letters going
'in' places the shortened word inside the president's name

blocks.note: Abe Lincoln, sixteenth US president
taken as written before halving

explanation.surface: A brick for a building project, half finished in the city of Lincoln.
explanation.walkthrough: Lincoln reads as the English cathedral city, but it is Abraham Lincoln.
explanation.definitionFit: Adobe is sun-dried clay brick used in construction, especially in the American Southwest.

clue.text: Red-faced state is never-ending

indicators.note: something never-ending has no end, so the last letter is dropped

blocks.note: a US state

explanation.surface: Someone's flushed condition is permanent.
explanation.walkthrough: 'State' looks like condition, but it is the American state.
explanation.definitionFit: Florid describes a complexion that is ruddy or flushed.

clue.text: Garden plant type of yucca hospital regularly wanted

indicators.note: 'regularly' asks for letters at an even interval, every other one

blocks.note: the second, fourth, sixth and so on letters of these words

explanation.surface: A gardener is after a yucca for the hospital grounds.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Yucca' and 'garden plant' tempt you to look for a plant name, but yucca is just a source of letters.
explanation.definitionFit: The fuchsia is a popular flowering shrub grown in gardens for its drooping blooms.

clue.text: Deadlock that is broken by politician: fool!

indicators.note: something broken by another thing is split open so that thing sits inside

blocks.note: i.e., Latin id est
Member of Parliament
a plain synonym

explanation.surface: A political stalemate, broken by one MP who is denounced as a fool.
explanation.definitionFit: An impasse is a situation where no progress is possible, a stalemate.

clue.text: Hate side losing openers before cricket match

indicators.note: the openers are the first letters, and losing them strips them off
'before' puts one piece ahead of the next

blocks.note: taken as written before losing letters
a Test is an international cricket match

explanation.surface: A cricket team hates losing its opening batsmen before a big match.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Openers' suggests opening batsmen, but it means the first two letters of the word.
explanation.definitionFit: To detest is to loathe intensely, a synonym for hate as a verb.

clue.text: Whisky adulterated by the French? With this one may get hammered

definitions.text: With this one may get hammered

indicators.note: adulterated drink has something mixed into it, so a piece is put inside

blocks.note: malt is a whisky
French for the

explanation.surface: Spiked whisky gets you hammered.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hammered' fits the drinking scene as drunk, but the definition means struck with this tool.
explanation.definitionFit: A mallet is a wooden hammer, so with it something is literally hammered.

clue.text: What's initially curtailing run after muscle pain?

definitions.text: What's initially curtailing run after muscle pain?

indicators.note: 'initially' asks for the first letter of each following word

blocks.note: the opening letter of each of these five words

explanation.surface: A runner asks what cut short their run after a muscle pain.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is also the definition: a muscle pain that cuts a run short.
explanation.definitionFit: A cramp is a sudden painful muscle spasm, which can stop a runner.

clue.text: Praise article by Conservative right

blocks.note: the indefinite article
C is the abbreviation for Conservative
a claim is a right to something

explanation.surface: A newspaper article by a Conservative praises the right.
explanation.definitionFit: To acclaim is to praise enthusiastically and publicly.

clue.text: Provide food consumed in common room initially

indicators.note: 'initially' asks for the first letter of each of the two words before it
'in' places the eating word inside the initials

blocks.note: the opening letters of both words
consumed means ate

explanation.surface: Someone supplies food that is eaten in the common room.
explanation.definitionFit: To cater is to supply food and drink, for example at an event.

clue.text: Power oared boat using mass for energy

indicators.note: 'using' one thing for another means swapping it in as a replacement
'for' here means in place of, marking the letter that is swapped out

blocks.note: a rowing eight has eight oars
M is the symbol for mass
E is the symbol for energy

explanation.surface: A powerful rowing boat trades mass for energy.
explanation.walkthrough: The physics words are just letter symbols; the M replaces the E at the front of the boat.
explanation.definitionFit: Might is strength or force, a synonym for power.

clue.text: Team spilling the beans is hilarious

blocks.note: a side is a team
to split is slang for to inform or betray a secret

explanation.surface: A team letting out its secrets is a laugh.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Split' in British slang means to inform on someone, so spilling the beans is splitting.
explanation.definitionFit: Something side-splitting makes you laugh so hard your sides hurt, which is to say very funny.

clue.text: Area yielded a variety of succulent

blocks.note: A is the abbreviation for area
yielded means gave way or gave up

explanation.surface: A patch of ground produced a kind of succulent plant.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Yielded' suggests a crop producing, but it means gave.
explanation.definitionFit: The agave is a spiky succulent plant of the Americas, source of tequila.

clue.text: Other ranks trapped by river in spate

indicators.note: something trapped is held inside, so one piece sits within the other

blocks.note: the Trent is a major English river
OR is the military abbreviation for other ranks, soldiers who are not officers

explanation.surface: Soldiers are cut off by a river in flood.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In spate' looks like part of the surface's flood, but 'in' is the link and spate alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A spate is a sudden flood or rush, and a torrent is a violent rushing stream.
